restructurings.reason: Window 9 has been eliminated. Its staffing budget was reassigned to fund your promotion, and its clerk is now available for reassignment, possibly to you.
The Sub-Archive is closed for an audit. A single personnel file has been found in two places at once, and both of them are yours.

restructurings.title: Customer Experience Hub
restructurings.reason: The Pneumatic Tube Exchange and Window 9 have merged into one Customer Experience Hub, to save compliant employees like you a walk. Please queue in both lines.

restructurings.title: Exchange, second delivery
restructurings.reason: After the incident at your review, all inter-office mail is routed past your desk twice. PAL is sure you have nothing to hide.

restructurings.title: Sub-Archive, via the ducts
restructurings.reason: A duct entrance has been discovered above the Sub-Archive. Facilities has added it to your route so everyone can stop pretending it is not there.
Records has been restructured overnight. Nothing has changed. Please act surprised, and report anyone who does not.

encounters.title: A Capsule from Yourself
encounters.flavor_text: A brass capsule thunks into the tray with your name on it, in your handwriting. The postmark is next Thursday. Inside is a note that says DO NOT OPEN THE OTHER ONE, and a second, smaller capsule, also addressed to you, sealed with Records tape. PAL chimes. "Reminder: correspondence with yourself requires a Self-Correspondence Permit."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker at a brass pneumatic tube terminal holding a capsule in each hand, one large and one small, a curl of postmarked paper unrolling between them, a wall of gleaming brass tubes rising behind like organ pipes, carbon blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Open the other one anyway
choices.intent: Your future self is not the boss of you. Yet.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check; future-you sealed it for a reason.

success.text: Inside is a list of three names in your handwriting: Dale, the Supervisor, and you. One has a tick beside it. The tick is smudged, as if you were in a hurry next Thursday.

failure.text: It is a Records confetti charge. You spend an hour picking paper dots out of your collar while PAL logs one count of Unauthorized Self-Correspondence.

choices.label: Ask Pip to open it for you
choices.intent: Pip trusts you. Pip would open anything you asked him to.
choices.risk_hint: Requires Pip's trust. Certain outcome; Pip takes the risk and you take the guilt.

success.text: Pip opens it without a second thought, because you asked. It is a Records confetti charge. He loses an eyebrow, gains a commendation for Bravery in Correspondence, and thanks you. Of course he thanks you.

choices.label: Readdress it to last Tuesday
choices.intent: If future-you can write to you, you can write to past-you.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Postage across time costs a Form.

success.text: The tube accepts it with a satisfied gulp. You have a sudden feeling that your past self just made a slightly better choice, though you cannot recall which one.

choices.label: Turn both capsules in to PAL
choices.intent: Self-correspondence is irregular. Be regular.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your file improves; your future self is ignored.

success.text: PAL thanks you for reporting Unauthorized Self-Correspondence. Both capsules are shredded unread. Somewhere next Thursday, you sigh.

encounters.title: The Jam in Tube 14
encounters.flavor_text: Tube 14 is groaning. Something large is stuck in it, somewhere between Payroll and the ceiling. A muffled voice drifts out of the brass: "Hello? It's Kevin. Most of me." Beside the tube hangs an emergency kit containing a fire axe, a flare, and a neatly folded towel. A placard reads: EMPLOYEES ARE NOT CAPSULES.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a fat brass pneumatic tube bulging in one round lump along its length, a worker with one ear pressed to the brass, an open emergency kit on the wall holding a red axe, a flare and a neatly folded striped towel, steam curling from a joint, safety-orange and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Brace your feet and pull
choices.intent: Open the hatch and haul on whatever you can reach.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. Tubes pull back. Failure is a Successor.

success.text: Out comes a shoe, a lanyard, and a gust of very grateful air. Kevin's voice thanks you from two tubes over, already being delivered somewhere else. He owes you one, if he can ever stay still long enough to pay.

failure.text: The tube pulls harder. Employee #4471 has been delivered to Accounts Receivable, folded neatly. Your Successor signs for you.

choices.label: Crank the pressure valve
choices.intent: Whatever is stuck can simply be delivered faster.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check; tampering with the Exchange is logged.

success.text: Kevin is delivered, at speed, to a department you cannot pronounce. A minute later a capsule arrives holding a thank-you card and two Forms with a faint tread mark on them.

failure.text: Every capsule in the Exchange fires at once. You are knee-deep in lunches, memos and evidence, and Dispatch would like a short, friendly conversation.

choices.label: File a maintenance ticket
choices.intent: There is a procedure for this. There is a procedure for everything.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Costs a Form. Kevin waits.

success.text: Maintenance will arrive in six to eight weeks. From inside Tube 14, Kevin says that's fine. He sounds like a man who has been here before, and will be here again.

choices.label: Drop in through the duct above Tube 14
choices.intent: Marguerite's routes pass right over the jam.
choices.risk_hint: Requires knowing the ducts. Routine Initiative check, very tight squeeze.

success.text: You lower yourself headfirst, unhook a snagged belt loop, and wriggle back up before anyone looks. Below you, Kevin whooshes away to freedom, yelling thanks. You keep the towel. It feels important.

failure.text: You free Kevin, and the tube takes your shoes as payment. Facilities finds you in your socks above the Exchange and asks a great many questions.

encounters.title: Problem Mail
encounters.flavor_text: Dispatcher Fenwick wears sleeve garters and a headset, and sorts capsules into two chutes: DELIVER and PROBLEM. PROBLEM drops straight into the incinerator. You watch a capsule with your employee number slide toward the PROBLEM chute. Fenwick watches you watching it. "Happens to everyone eventually," he says. "Some people just get there early."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a lean dispatcher in sleeve garters and a headset standing between two brass chutes, one glowing warm orange from a furnace below, his hand resting on a capsule sliding toward the glow, a worker reaching from the side, oxblood and safety-orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Snatch your capsule off the chute
choices.intent: Whatever is in it is yours, by definition.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Fenwick has fast hands.

success.text: It is your own Suspicion report, unfiled. You read it in a stall: they know about the badge photo. You burn it yourself, which feels like freedom and also like destroying evidence.

failure.text: Fenwick's hand closes over yours, gently. "Problem mail," he says, "includes people who touch problem mail." He writes your number on a fresh capsule.

choices.label: Show him the bent paperclip
choices.intent: The Front left you a paperclip shaped like a fist. Maybe Fenwick knows it.
choices.risk_hint: Requires Stapler Liberation Front contact. Certain outcome; Front favors are never free.

success.text: Fenwick glances at the paperclip. Without changing expression he moves your capsule to DELIVER and slips you a second one marked FOR THE FRONT. "Pass it on," he murmurs. "And never ask what's in it."

choices.label: Swap the chute labels
choices.intent: For a few minutes, let every problem get delivered.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Tinkering check; the labels are riveted on.

success.text: For six glorious minutes every problem gets delivered. Complaints reach their departments. A memo about the holiday toy shipment reaches Product Safety. The Exchange will never be the same, and neither will your file.

failure.text: The rivets pop the wrong way. The incinerator chute now reads DELIVER, and so, briefly, does your sleeve.

choices.label: Let it go down the chute
choices.intent: Some problems solve themselves, at roughly nine hundred degrees.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Whatever it was, it's warmth now.

success.text: Your capsule drops with a cheerful whoosh. Fenwick tips his visor. Whatever was in it was a problem, and now it is heating the Exchange.

encounters.title: Interdepartmental Romance
encounters.flavor_text: A pink capsule has circled the Exchange nine times, unable to land. It is a letter from Accounts Payable to Accounts Receivable, who have been forbidden to merge since the Restructuring of '88. Policy says it must be destroyed. The capsule is scented with lavender. The prose, visible through the glass, is frankly beautiful.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a pink glass capsule looping through a tangle of brass tubes trailing a faint lavender shimmer, two office doors far apart on opposite walls with silhouettes leaning wistfully in each doorway, a worker below catching the capsule, manila and fluorescent green palette with one pink accent, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Deliver it by hand
choices.intent: Love should arrive. Even in Records.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Discretion check. Unauthorized delivery is noticed.

success.text: Receivable reads it in silence and sends back one capsule: YES. By morning the two departments share a coffee pot, against every policy, and both of them remember your name fondly.

failure.text: The capsule pops open mid-delivery. PAL reads the letter aloud to the whole floor as a teachable moment. Nobody involved will ever forgive anyone.

choices.label: File a Merger Request for them
choices.intent: Make it official. Paperwork can be romantic.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check; merger forms cost two Forms.

success.text: The merger is approved on a technicality you will be asked about later. Accounts Payable-and-Receivable invites you to the ceremony, a budget meeting where refreshments are promised.

failure.text: The request is denied and both departments are rightsized as a precaution. The letter is filed under EVIDENCE, with your name as the submitting clerk.

choices.label: Unlock the service door between them
choices.intent: Marguerite's master key opens every door. Even this one.
choices.risk_hint: Requires the master key. Certain outcome; a sealed door opening gets noticed.

success.text: The service door between Payable and Receivable has been sealed since '88. The key turns like it has been waiting. You slide the letter through and leave the door ajar. By lunch the hinges have been oiled from both sides.

choices.label: Destroy it, per Merger Policy 9
choices.intent: Rules are rules, and this one has a number.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL approves; the Exchange smells of lavender for days.

success.text: PAL commends your adherence to Merger Policy 9. The capsule's lavender lingers in the Exchange for days, like a reproach nobody else seems to smell.

encounters.title: Your Permanent Record
encounters.flavor_text: Drawer 4471 holds your personnel file. It is nine inches thick. It includes your childhood dental records, a transcript of a dream you had on Tuesday, and a review dated next spring that says you "showed real promise before the incident." A blood-pressure cuff is clipped to the drawer. It inflates gently as you read, and records the numbers in the file.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker standing at an open filing drawer holding an enormously thick manila folder, a blood-pressure cuff wrapped around one arm connected by a rubber tube to a round dial gauge on the cabinet, the needle swinging high, one bare bulb swinging overhead, endless cabinets fading into gloom, manila and carbon blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Read about the incident
choices.intent: If something is going to happen to you, you want the details.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. The cuff is watching your pulse.

success.text: The incident is described in full: which door, which Thursday, which coworker. Forewarned is not quite forearmed, but it is at least a sleeve.

failure.text: The incident pages are redacted with a marker that smells of oranges. In the margin, in your handwriting, someone has written: sorry.

choices.label: Submit corrections in triplicate
choices.intent: Fix your record properly. There's a form for it.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check; triplicate costs two Forms.

success.text: Corrections accepted. The dream transcript is removed, the dental records are amended, and the spring review now ends after "showed real promise." Full stop.

failure.text: Your corrections are filed as a new section titled ATTEMPTED CORRECTIONS. The file is now ten inches thick, and the cuff tightens.

choices.label: Refile it under the scratched-out badge
choices.intent: You are wearing a dead man's badge. Let him carry your record too.
choices.risk_hint: Requires the dead man's badge. Certain outcome; it is a strange thing to do to a stranger.

success.text: You reshelve your file under the badge's number. Your record now belongs to someone the Company believes is already reassigned. You feel lighter, and a little haunted.

choices.label: Walk out with the whole file
choices.intent: No file, no record. No record, no problem.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Discretion check. It weighs as much as a toddler.

success.text: You leave with yourself under your arm. Officially you no longer have a record, which means you were never hired, which means your parking validation is void.

failure.text: The file is chained to the drawer, the drawer to the floor, and the floor to the Company. Archivists find you hugging it and do not ask why.

encounters.title: Alphabetizing Since 1974
encounters.flavor_text: In aisle A an elderly clerk in a cardigan is alphabetizing one drawer. He has been doing it since 1974. "Each time I finish," Mr. Pemberton explains, "somebody adds a file under A." He shows you his assignment slip. It is a Wellness evaluation: Persistence Under Pointless Conditions. The box marked END OF TEST has never been checked.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a gentle elderly clerk in a cardigan and sleeve garters fingering through a single open file drawer with infinite patience, a faded assignment slip in his other hand, a worker leaning in beside him, dust motes drifting in the beam of one bulb, manila and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Tell him the test is over
choices.intent: Somebody should. It has been fifty years.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. He has heard it before.

success.text: He reads the slip three times, then folds it carefully into his pocket. "Well," he says. "Well, well." He hands you the drawer key and walks toward the elevator, straight-backed, to find out what year it is.

failure.text: He thanks you kindly and keeps filing. "They always send someone to say it's over," he says. "That's part of the test." He files you, gently, under N for New.

choices.label: Check END OF TEST yourself
choices.intent: If nobody will sign him out, you will.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check; forging a proctor's mark costs a Form.

success.text: You tick the box with a steady hand. Somewhere a bell that has waited fifty years finally rings. PAL announces Mr. Pemberton's retirement, and your new reputation for initiative.

failure.text: The pen leaks. END OF TEST becomes a large blot shaped, upsettingly, like a mushroom cloud. Mr. Pemberton files the blot under M.

choices.label: Sit down and help him file
choices.intent: Maybe the kind thing is simply company.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. An hour of your shift, gone somewhere peaceful.

success.text: You spend an hour filing beside him. It is the calmest hour you have had in the building. When you leave, the drawer has two new files under A, and one of them is yours.

choices.label: Correct Pemberton's score in red
choices.intent: Your Red Pen profile grants you one correction. Use it for the man who has been waiting since 1974.
choices.risk_hint: Requires Red Pen profile. Risky Compliance check: the answer key belongs to Wellness.

success.text: You draw a red line through INCOMPLETE and write PASSED. Pemberton sets his index cards down, very gently, as if the cabinet might wake. His retirement notice prints in your name, under PROCTOR. 'You should come to my garden,' he says. The camera above the drawer swivels toward you.

failure.text: Your red correction feeds back through the scoring machine and lands on your own personnel file: RETEST REQUIRED. Pemberton offers you a chair. 'I can show you how to wait without forgetting what you are waiting for,' he says.

encounters.title: The Cabinet Marked DESTROY
encounters.flavor_text: At the end of aisle Q stands a grey cabinet stenciled DESTROY. It is full. Every file inside has been stamped DESTROYED and then very carefully kept. A ballpoint pen rests on top, angled exactly at the second drawer. People say the Society for Accurate Minutes leaves its pens that way, and people who say so tend to be reassigned.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a tall grey filing cabinet alone at the end of a long dim aisle, drawers bulging with folders, a single ballpoint pen balanced on top pointing at the second drawer, a worker approaching with a flashlight, deep shadows between the aisles, carbon blue and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Open the second drawer
choices.intent: The pen is pointing. You'd be rude to ignore it.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. Somebody may be keeping watch on the cabinet.

success.text: Drawer two holds the real minutes of every Board meeting since the Founder was a whole person. You read about the Toy Division budget until your hands go cold, then take one page.

failure.text: The drawer is wired to a bell. Archivists arrive with flashlights. You explain you were destroying the files, so they cheerfully help you finish the job.

choices.label: Leave your own pen beside theirs
choices.intent: Angle it the same way. See who answers.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Discretion check. Costs a Form, wrapped around the pen as a note.

success.text: When you come back, your pen has been swapped for a better one and a folded note: Thursday. Aisle Q. Bring nothing written down. The Society for Accurate Minutes has noticed you.

failure.text: Your pen has been replaced with a pencil and a note that reads: Not yet. An archivist you have never seen before nods at you on the way out.

choices.label: Report the angled pens to Records Security
choices.intent: A secret society is meeting in your department. That is a reportable event.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL is grateful. The Society keeps minutes.

success.text: Records Security confiscates every angled pen in the Sub-Archive. Somewhere in aisle Q an elderly voice says your full name, once, slowly, as if writing it down.

choices.label: Open the drawer with your Paperclip result
choices.intent: Your test paperclip fits a keyhole. Maybe flexibility was a job qualification all along.
choices.risk_hint: Requires Paperclip profile. Risky Discretion check; archivists regard bending as tampering.

success.text: The clip opens the drawer. Inside are personnel records filed under EQUIPMENT, including yours. A footnote reads: FLEXIBLE PERSONNEL MAY BE REPURPOSED WITHOUT NOTICE. You take the page. On your way out, your visitor badge is already labeled TOOL.

failure.text: The paperclip snaps inside the lock. The drawer stamps your file REPAIR REQUESTED. PAL thanks you for volunteering as a replacement hinge. You escape before Facilities arrives with its measuring tape.

encounters.title: The Union Archive
encounters.flavor_text: Behind a false cabinet lies a cave of shredded paper, painstakingly reassembled. Gus sits under a reading lamp in his cardigan and half-moon glasses, tweezers in one claw. "Everything they shred, we rebuild," he says. "Takes a while. We have time. We have, frankly, more time than anyone." Strips of memo are pinned to every wall like moths.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a giant cockroach in a mustard cardigan and half-moon reading glasses hunched at a desk under a green-shaded lamp, delicately piecing paper strips together with tweezers, walls papered with reassembled memos, a worker peering in through a gap behind a swung-open filing cabinet, warm lamplight against deep shadow, manila and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Pull up a stool and help
choices.intent: Many hands, or claws, make light work.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. The strips are very small.

success.text: Three hours, one memo: Re: Snuggle Sentinel holiday shipment, quantity forty thousand. Gus files it under EVIDENCE with a claw that shakes, just slightly.

failure.text: You tape the memo together in the wrong order. It now says the Roach Union is a subsidiary of the Toy Division. Gus is extremely polite about it.

choices.label: Ask Gus what the Union has on you
choices.intent: You're a friend of the Union. Friends get to see their files.
choices.risk_hint: Requires being a Roach Union ally. Certain outcome; Union business gets you watched.

success.text: Gus slides over a folder labeled 4471, thicker than the Company's. "Union keeps better records," he says. Inside is the name of whoever requested your hire. It is your own signature.

choices.label: Tip off Pest Control
choices.intent: This is a lot of shredded evidence and one very large insect.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL is thrilled. The Union never forgets.

success.text: Pest Control floods the archive with a cheerful lemon-scented fog. When it clears, the reassembled papers are confetti again. Gus is gone. His reading lamp is still warm.

choices.label: Use your Shredder clearance as cover
choices.intent: Defense trusts you to dispose of paper. Gus can reconstruct what you bring him, if you keep the pieces.
choices.risk_hint: Requires Shredder profile. Risky Discretion check; Defense tracks every disposed sheet.

success.text: You sign out the confiscated union roster as DESTROYED and feed the pieces to Gus through a service hatch. He spends the night restoring names, not just evidence. He pauses over one: Kevin, still listed as a dues-paying member. The disposal camera catches your sleeve.

failure.text: Defense counts the pages before you can pass them over. Gus quietly burns his list of safe meeting rooms so nobody else will be caught. 'You meant well,' he says, which is somehow worse than an accusation.

encounters.title: Flawless Paperwork
encounters.flavor_text: The next applicant is a six-foot cockroach in a neat navy blazer. Her name is Beverly. She is applying for your job, specifically, by employee number. Her paperwork is flawless: notarized, laminated, cross-referenced. Your own application, you remember, had a coffee ring on it. PAL hums, "Remember to approve the most qualified candidate!"
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a poised six-foot cockroach in a navy blazer and pearl earrings sliding a stack of glossy laminated documents through a booth drawer, a sweating worker behind thick glass holding a brass stamp, a long queue curling away behind her, carbon blue and safety-orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Approve her. She's better at it.
choices.intent: Honesty, and the paperwork, demand it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. You lose your desk; she remembers who was fair.

success.text: Beverly is hired. You are moved to the desk behind your desk. She turns out to be an excellent manager, and she always remembers who stamped her application.

choices.label: Find a flaw and deny her
choices.intent: There's always something. A comma. A crease.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. If there's no flaw, you deny her anyway.

success.text: You find a stray comma inside the laminate. Beverly takes her application back with great dignity and one long look. Word travels fast under the baseboards.

failure.text: There is no flaw. You deny her anyway. PAL notes an Irregular Rejection, and Beverly notes your badge number in a small leather book.

choices.label: Slide her a union card instead
choices.intent: A position with collective bargaining beats a position with you in it.
choices.risk_hint: Requires Roach Union membership. Routine Rapport check; dues cost a Form.

success.text: Beverly's antennae lift. "Organizing," she says. "Now that is a career." She withdraws her application for your job and files a grievance against Window 9 instead.

failure.text: She already has a union card. She has two. She thanks you warmly and still wants your job, and now she knows you're soft.

choices.label: Staple Beverly's application to yours
choices.intent: Your Stapler classification says people belong together. Make PAL process you as one employment unit.
choices.risk_hint: Requires Stapler profile. Certain outcome; you become legally inseparable colleagues.

success.text: You staple the two applications together. PAL cannot separate them without Form D: Division of Personnel. Beverly gets the job and insists your name stays beside hers on the door. The first invoice for her excellent work is charged to you. 'We can appeal together,' she says.

encounters.title: The Small Box on Line 12
encounters.flavor_text: Dr. Halvorsen is at your window, clipboard hugged to her chest. Her form requests transfer to Surface Wellness, where the tests have answers. Line 12, in very small type: Vacancy to be filled by the processing officer. That is you. She sees you read it. "It is a very small box," she says quietly. "I have been looking at it for eleven years."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a brisk psychologist in cat-eye glasses and a lab coat over a cardigan standing at a thick glass booth window, clutching an enormous clipboard, one transfer form lying in the brass drawer between her and a worker holding a stamp, both looking down at the same tiny line, fluorescent green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Approve it and take the vacancy
choices.intent: She has waited eleven years. You can wear a lab coat.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. She goes free; the Vault gets a new proctor.

success.text: Her transfer goes through with a soft pneumatic sigh. She squeezes your hand and leaves by an elevator going up. An hour later a lab coat in your size arrives by tube.

choices.label: Stamp it REASSIGNED
choices.intent: You cannot afford her freedom. You are sorry. You are mostly sorry.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Safe for you. Not for her.

success.text: She nods as if she expected exactly this, and it is the nod that stays with you. She leaves her pen in your drawer. It is a very good pen.

choices.label: Amend line 12 to name the Supervisor
choices.intent: Nobody reads line 12. That is the whole point of line 12.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Discretion check; amendments cost a Form.

success.text: The form now names your Supervisor as her replacement. It is approved at once, because nobody reads line 12. Somewhere above, a grey three-piece suit receives a lab coat.

failure.text: The amendment is spotted by a clerk who reads line 12 for fun. You and Dr. Halvorsen are both invited to a short, friendly conversation.

choices.label: Give back the envelope she slipped you
choices.intent: At Orientation she handed you a sealed envelope. Maybe it was meant for this.
choices.risk_hint: Requires Halvorsen's envelope. Certain outcome; you spend your one secret on her.

success.text: Inside is a blank exemption, pre-signed. She stares at it, then at you. "I gave that to you," she says, "for you." She takes the transfer anyway, and line 12 stays empty.

encounters.title: Dale Requests a Transfer
encounters.flavor_text: Dale from Compliance reaches the front of the queue, mustache freshly combed. His form requests transfer to any department "at least two floors from Employee 4471." Under REASON he has written Personal, crossed it out, written Professional, and crossed that out too. He does not quite meet your eyes. "Just stamp it," he says. "Please. For both of us."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a mild mustached man in a short-sleeved shirt and clip-on tie at a thick glass booth window, eyes cast sideways, pushing a form through the drawer with two fingers, a worker behind the glass holding a brass stamp aloft and hesitating, a long queue fading into the distance, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp it APPROVED
choices.intent: If he wants distance, give him distance.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. You lose a friend, or an informant, or both.

success.text: Dale exhales like a man surfacing. "You're all right, 4471," he says, and leaves a folded note in the drawer: the name of his society, in a code you cannot read yet.

choices.label: Hold the stamp and ask him why
choices.intent: You want the real reason before you decide.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Dale is better at secrets than he looks.

success.text: Dale leans close to the glass. "Somebody upstairs asked me to report on you," he whispers. "I've been telling them you're boring. You are making that very hard." He takes his form back.

failure.text: Dale stiffens. "Noted," he says, and writes something down. It is the first time you have ever seen Dale write anything that was not a signature.

choices.label: Confess you signed his name
choices.intent: At the visitor log, you signed as Dale. He deserves to hear it from you.
choices.risk_hint: Requires having forged Dale. Certain outcome; confessions are logged.

success.text: Dale is silent a long time. Then he laughs, once, helplessly. "Everybody signs as Dale," he says. "I have nineteen versions of myself on file." He tears up his transfer.

choices.label: Approve it, to the Toy Division
choices.intent: He wanted two floors. The Proving Grounds are two floors down.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The Supervisor likes initiative; Dale will not.

success.text: You tick Proving Grounds, Level -2, and slide the form through. Dale thanks you. He will not thank you later. The Supervisor notes your initiative with a small, cold smile.

failure.text: Dale reads the destination before it reaches the drawer. "Ah," he says. That is all he says. He goes anyway, and he remembers.

encounters.title: The Double-Sided Stamp
encounters.flavor_text: Your stamp is brass, heavy and double-sided: APPROVED on one face, REASSIGNED on the other. The handle has a worn spot where a thumb can tell which is which. The next applicant is an elderly man asking to visit his old desk one last time. PAL speaks softly. "Today's quota is balanced. Every yes requires a no."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a close view of a hand gripping a heavy two-faced brass stamp above an ink pad, the thumb resting on a polished worn spot, an elderly man in a hat waiting hopefully on the far side of thick glass, a ticking wall clock above, safety-orange and carbon blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Learn the feel of the worn spot
choices.intent: Know which face is down before it lands.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Vigilance check. Getting it wrong is getting it wrong on someone.

success.text: You find the spot. From now on every stamp lands exactly as you mean it, which is more than the last clerk managed. The old man visits his desk and sits at it for a while.

failure.text: You stamp the old man REASSIGNED by accident. He thanks you anyway. He says he has always wanted to see the moon.

choices.label: Approve him, and deny your own leave request
choices.intent: The quota wants a no. Give it your vacation.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your week off is gone, and PAL notices.

success.text: Quota balanced. The old man sits at his desk, smiling. Your own leave request, filed this morning, now reads REASSIGNED in fresh ink. PAL is confused, which is the closest PAL gets to respect.

choices.label: File down the REASSIGNED face
choices.intent: A stamp that can only say yes.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check; defacing Company brass is noticed.

success.text: With a nail file and patience, REASSIGNED becomes a smooth brass oval. Every stamp you give today is a yes or a blank, and blanks, it turns out, are processed as yes.

failure.text: You file through the wrong face. Your stamp now reads only REASSIGNED, in beautiful mirror-bright letters, and the queue has seen you do it.

choices.label: Keep the quota: yes, no, yes, no
choices.intent: It isn't your rule. It's only your hand.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your quota is perfect; something else is not.

success.text: Yes, no, yes, no. By noon you have a rhythm, and by two you have stopped looking at faces. PAL calls this flow. The old man was a no.

encounters.title: The Suggestion Tube
encounters.flavor_text: A new sky-blue tube has been bolted beside the Exchange, with a brass slot for Anonymous Suggestions. Every capsule it swallows pops out upstairs on the Supervisor's desk, beside a magnifying glass and a stack of handwriting samples. Pip is standing at the slot with a folded note that reads, in his big round letters, MAYBE FEWER REASSIGNMENTS? "It's anonymous," he tells you happily.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of an eager young intern in an oversized sweater raising a folded note toward a brass slot in a sky-blue pneumatic tube, the tube climbing up through the ceiling toward a distant desk lamp and a magnifying glass, a worker beside him reaching out a hand, carbon blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Let Pip post it
choices.intent: It's his suggestion. It's a good suggestion. It is his problem.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Pip's honesty, Pip's consequences.

success.text: The tube gulps Pip's note. Upstairs, a magnifying glass is lifted. By lunch Pip has been invited to a Suggestion Follow-Up Session, and he is thrilled to finally be heard.

choices.label: Copy it out in your own handwriting
choices.intent: If somebody is going to be matched to that note, let it be someone who saw it coming.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The heat lands on you instead of Pip.

success.text: You copy MAYBE FEWER REASSIGNMENTS? in your own hand and post it before he can. Pip pockets his note, puzzled. By lunch your handwriting has been matched, and PAL has scheduled a chat about your enthusiasm.

choices.label: Swap in a note praising PAL
choices.intent: A suggestion box only wants one kind of suggestion. Give it that.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check; the decoy costs a Form of good paper.

success.text: Pip's note slides up your sleeve and a glowing tribute to PAL's lighting choices drops into the slot. PAL is so moved it reads the suggestion aloud over the Exchange speakers. Pip is confused, and safe.

failure.text: Pip notices the swap and asks, loudly and kindly, why you have his note. Dispatcher Fenwick hears. So, as far as anyone can tell, does the tube.

choices.label: Post the HELP your hand wrote
choices.intent: At Orientation your hand wrote HELP on the survey and it would not erase. Let it go where it was aimed.
choices.risk_hint: Requires the HELP from your survey. Certain outcome; the word goes upstairs, and so does your handwriting.

success.text: Your pen writes HELP again before you can stop it, so you post that. Upstairs the magnifying glass matches it to no one, because HELP never matches anyone. In the fuss Pip forgets his own note, and for one afternoon the Supervisor's smile reaches something.

encounters.title: Marguerite's Freight Manifest
encounters.flavor_text: After hours, the Exchange's old freight tube wakes up with a cough. Marguerite is loading it: a mop, a bucket, a crate of toner, and a man in a cardigan folded up very small, who is due to be reassigned at nine tomorrow morning. She holds out a clipboard without looking at you. "Freight needs a countersignature," she says. "Just your initials. Mops don't ask questions."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a weathered night janitor in grey coveralls and a headscarf holding out a clipboard beside a wide brass freight tube, a mop, a bucket and a wooden crate lined up at its open hatch, a mild man in a cardigan curled up neatly inside the hatch, night-shift fluorescent green and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Initial the manifest
choices.intent: Your initials are small. His future is not.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your initials are now on a crate containing a person.

success.text: You initial it. The crate leaves with a long, polite whoosh toward a loading dock Marguerite swears is upstairs. She tucks a folded scrap of duct map into your breast pocket and pats it twice.

choices.label: List him on the manifest as toner
choices.intent: Nobody in the history of Records has ever audited toner.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check; a corrected manifest costs a Form.

success.text: The manifest now records thirteen cartons of toner, one unusually warm. Marguerite whistles low and adds your name to a very short list she keeps inside her headscarf.

failure.text: The freight scale reads one hundred and sixty pounds of toner. The night auditor raises an eyebrow and begins a form of his own, very slowly, enjoying it.

choices.label: Ride one stop to see where it goes
choices.intent: She owes you for the pens. You would like to know where freight really ends up.
choices.risk_hint: Requires Marguerite's debt. Certain outcome; tube travel is hard on the nerves, and it spends her favor.

success.text: She folds you in beside the man in the cardigan, who offers you half a sandwich. One stop later you see where freight really goes: a dim dock with a hand-painted arrow pointing up. She hauls you back out. "Now we're even," she says, and you are not sure you are.

choices.label: Report the freight to PAL
choices.intent: A person is not freight. Also, you would like to keep your job.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL is grateful. Marguerite has a long memory and a longer mop.

success.text: PAL thanks you warmly. The crate is opened on the dock, the man in the cardigan is reassigned on schedule, and Marguerite mops the same square of floor outside your booth for the rest of the night, watching you.

encounters.title: The Tube That Goes Up
encounters.flavor_text: Behind a riveted panel in the Exchange's oldest wall, one tube runs the wrong way. Capsules fed into it rise, and the air sighing down it smells of cut grass and parking lot. Fenwick swears nothing alive has ever come back down. Pip has already climbed onto the intake ledge. "Somebody should test it," he says, tightening his lanyards. "I'm very expendable. It says so on my badge."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a single brass tube rising straight up through a dim wall of riveted pipes toward a small square of blue daylight far above, a cowlicked young intern in a big sweater perched on the intake ledge gripping his lanyards, a worker reaching up to tug his sleeve, safety orange and carbon blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Pull Pip down and go yourself
choices.intent: If anyone is going up a mystery tube today, it should be someone with Successors on file.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Initiative check. The tube is fast, and failure is a Successor.

success.text: You rocket up forty floors of brass and come to rest against a grille. Through it you see sky, actual sky, and a security guard eating a sandwich. Then the pressure reverses, politely, and you are returned to the Exchange with grass on your shoes and the route in your head.

failure.text: Halfway up, the tube reconsiders. Your Successor is thawed by lunch and handed a capsule containing your shoes. PAL logs the incident as an unscheduled commute.

choices.label: Let Pip test it
choices.intent: He volunteered. He always volunteers. That is rather the problem.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Pip goes up; you find out what comes down.

success.text: Pip waves and is gone with a sound like a cork. Twenty minutes later he drops back into the down tray, windswept, holding a dandelion. "There's sky," he whispers. Then PAL invites him to a short, friendly conversation about where he has been.

choices.label: Send a capsule up with a message
choices.intent: If the tube goes somewhere real, somebody up there can read.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check; rigging a capsule to stay up costs a Form.

success.text: You weight a capsule and roll a note inside: SEND HELP, OR AT LEAST SANDWICHES. It rises and stays risen. Hours later a capsule drops down holding a parking stub dated today. Someone up there is reading.

failure.text: The capsule comes straight back down at speed and finds the Supervisor's coffee mug on its way past the dispatch desk. Pip helps you write the apology.

choices.label: Bolt the panel back on
choices.intent: Some tubes are behind panels for a reason. You may not want to know the reason.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Safe, sealed, and on your conscience.

success.text: You lift Pip down by the sweater and bolt the panel shut, one rivet at a time. The grass smell lingers for an hour, then the vents take it. PAL commends your attention to building integrity.

encounters.title: Mail for Kevin
encounters.flavor_text: The undeliverable tray is full of capsules for Kevin. A seed catalog. A get-well card from Accounts. A reminder that his dental cleaning is overdue, which seems optimistic. PAL has stamped each one FORWARD TO: PAPERLESS ROLE, and the tube for Paperless Role is a narrow slot that ends in a warm draft. The last capsule in the tray is ticking, gently, like a wristwatch.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker sorting a wire tray heaped with brass capsules and a seed catalog beside a narrow slot breathing a warm amber draft, one small capsule held up to the ear, wall of brass tubes curving overhead, manila and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Forward it all, per PAL
choices.intent: Kevin is in a paperless role now. Paper is for people with roles that have paper.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Tidy for your file, hard on your heart.

success.text: The capsules go into the warm draft one by one. The last one ticks all the way down until you cannot hear it. PAL thanks you for keeping Kevin's correspondence current.

choices.label: Open the ticking capsule
choices.intent: It is probably a watch. It is probably not anything else.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Vigilance check; opening another employee's mail gets noticed.

success.text: It is Kevin's wristwatch, still running, with a tiny map of the Exchange engraved on the back and a star scratched beside Tube 14. You strap it on. It runs four minutes fast, like Kevin did.

failure.text: It is a Records confetti charge, the same as everyone else's. Fenwick applauds slowly from the dispatch desk while you pick paper dots out of your eyebrows.

choices.label: Sign the get-well card yourself
choices.intent: Someone should. Nobody has. It has been circulating since spring.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. It costs you something to write it.

success.text: You write: Hope you are feeling more whole. It is the nicest sentence anyone in Records has written this year. By evening seven other clerks have signed beneath yours, very small.

choices.label: Keep his mail in your drawer
choices.intent: Filed under Pending Return. Kevin comes back, eventually, mostly.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. PAL does tidiness sweeps.

success.text: Kevin's mail goes into your bottom drawer, filed under Pending Return. When PAL asks, you say the tube was busy. Somewhere, someone feels slightly less paperless.

failure.text: PAL finds the drawer during a routine tidiness sweep. Kevin's mail is forwarded, and so is a short note about you.

encounters.title: The Successor Index
encounters.flavor_text: Aisle S ends in a card catalog of oak drawers, one per employee number. Yours slides open on its own. Behind your index card stand five more, B through F, each with a start date typed in red. Successor C's start date is tomorrow morning. A carbon slip is clipped to it: Pending outcome of Records placement. A pencil hangs on a string beside the drawer, freshly sharpened.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker staring into a long oak card-catalog drawer pulled open at chest height, a row of six index cards standing inside like headstones, a sharpened pencil dangling on a string, a single swinging bulb overhead and filing cabinets receding into haze, manila and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Erase tomorrow and write next year
choices.intent: It is a pencil. They left you a pencil.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Somebody three aisles over is listening for erasers.

success.text: The date erases cleanly, which is the frightening part. Next year looks good in your handwriting. The drawer closes itself with a satisfied click.

failure.text: The eraser goes through the card. A clerk three aisles over stops turning pages. A fresh card is typed for C at once, and the red date on it is this afternoon.

choices.label: Correct it to the date you overheard
choices.intent: Inside a wall at Orientation you heard two managers agree on a different start date.
choices.risk_hint: Requires the start date you overheard. Certain outcome; the correction is filed under your number.

success.text: You change C's date to the one you heard in the duct. The card accepts it at once: it was the real date all along, and somebody had been rushing it. You have a little longer than they wanted you to.

choices.label: Read Successor B's card
choices.intent: B is a bit ahead of you. B might have left notes.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check; some files read you back.

success.text: B's card lists your favorite sandwich, your worst fear and, under Notes, one word in B's own handwriting: Sorry. B was here before you, and B has already read yours.

failure.text: B's card is blank except for a fingerprint, which is yours. You spend the rest of your shift not thinking about it, loudly.

choices.label: Initial C's start date as approved
choices.intent: Cooperation with your own replacement is a sign of maturity.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL is proud of you. You are less sure.

success.text: You initial tomorrow. PAL plays a soft chime and marks you as Succession-Ready. The pencil swings gently on its string for a long time afterward.

encounters.title: The Inkblot Annex
encounters.flavor_text: Every inkblot answer ever given at Orientation is filed here, in drawers sorted by what people saw. The drawer for BUTTERFLY is enormous. The drawer for SUPERVISOR is locked. A clerk with a rubber thumb is moving cards from a thin drawer into the butterfly drawer, one at a time. "Harmonization," she says brightly. "Yours is on my cart. Shall I move it for you?"
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a cheerful clerk in a cardigan and a rubber thumb guard lifting an inkblot card from a narrow drawer toward an enormous overflowing drawer, rows of tiny symmetrical ink shapes fanned across a rolling cart, a worker leaning in with a wary look, carbon blue and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Let her harmonize your answer
choices.intent: Butterflies are lovely. Everyone agrees about butterflies.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your file relaxes; you are a little less sure what you saw.

success.text: Your answer becomes butterfly. You feel lighter and slightly vague. PAL's next chime calls you by a friendly nickname you have never been called before.

choices.label: Find the drawer for mushroom clouds
choices.intent: You said mushroom cloud at Orientation. Someone filed it somewhere.
choices.risk_hint: Requires your honest inkblot answer. Certain outcome; browsing restricted drawers is noticed.

success.text: The drawer is narrow and full: forty years of new hires who said the true thing. Dr. Halvorsen's initials are on every card. You copy down a dozen names that are still on payroll.

choices.label: Put Dale's card on the cart instead
choices.intent: Dale saw a door. Dale could stand to see a butterfly.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Her rubber thumb is very quick.

success.text: Dale's answer, which was DOOR, goes off to be harmonized in place of yours. Tomorrow Dale will see butterflies, and he will be happier, and you will know why.

failure.text: The clerk catches your wrist with her rubber thumb. Both cards go onto the cart, and a small note goes to Compliance, where Dale reads it first.

choices.label: Pocket a blank inkblot card
choices.intent: Every answer in here was the test. You would like to see the question.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Vigilance check; wait for her back to turn.

success.text: You slip a blank card into your jacket. Under your desk lamp it is only a smudge someone folded in half. Whatever anyone saw in it, they brought with them.

failure.text: The blank card is stuck to the one behind it, which is yours. Now your answer is in your pocket and PAL is asking, gently, where it went.

encounters.title: The Founding Charter
encounters.flavor_text: In a reading booth at the back of aisle F, a microfilm reader hums like a sleeping cat. The reel already threaded is the Company's founding charter, dated the year of the garage. It is three pages long. Page one promises to make the world safer. Page two promises to remember everyone's name. Page three has been copied so many times that it has worn away into grey weather.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker leaning into the hooded glow of a microfilm reader in a small wooden booth, a soft rectangle of light on the screen showing a faded garage workbench, film reels stacked on the ledge, filing cabinets fading into darkness behind, manila and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Enhance page three
choices.intent: The focus knob goes further than anyone has dared to turn it.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. The bulb is older than the Company.

success.text: With the focus all the way over, page three resolves: a promise that the Company will never make anything it would not hand to its own family, signed beneath a magnificent mustache drawn in ink.

failure.text: The bulb pops. The booth fills with the smell of hot film, and an archivist arrives to ask, very kindly, what you were trying to see.

choices.label: Match it to the chapter they skipped
choices.intent: You have seen this garage before, in the reel Orientation tried not to show you.
choices.risk_hint: Requires having seen the unlisted chapter. Certain outcome; splices leave fingerprints.

success.text: You know this garage. The charter's reel has a splice at the same frame the projector skipped. Behind the splice is a fourth page: a pencil sketch of a door marked with a stapler, and an arrow pointing up.

choices.label: Print a copy for the Society
choices.intent: Someone in here keeps minutes. They would want this.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check; a print request costs a Form.

success.text: The reader prints one warm grey copy. You leave it on top of the DESTROY cabinet in aisle Q. By morning it is gone, and a ballpoint pen on your desk is angled at you.

failure.text: The print request is routed to Records Security for approval, which is to say for reading. Your copy comes back stamped OUTDATED, with your name on the cover sheet.

choices.label: Rewind it and reshelve it
choices.intent: Some promises are private. Some promises are expired.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL approves; you walk away from page three.

success.text: You rewind the reel and shelve it under Restricted, Sentimental. PAL thanks you for respecting the Company's privacy, and the booth light clicks off behind you.

encounters.title: Forty-Two Years Overdue
encounters.flavor_text: The circulation desk in the Sub-Archive has a bell, a stamp pad and a librarian in a hairnet who has been waiting for you specifically. A book was checked out under employee number 4471 in the spring of '84 and never returned. The fine has compounded every minute since, payable by the current holder of the number. "It's very simple," she says, sliding the total under the bell. "You are 4471."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a stern librarian in a hairnet and cardigan behind a tall oak circulation desk, one finger resting on a silver bell, a long curling adding-machine tape spilling off the desk and across the floor toward a dismayed worker, carbon blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Pay the fine in Forms
choices.intent: It is not your debt. It is, however, your number.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Two Forms, and the book is yours.

success.text: She stamps PAID with relish and hands you the book: Safety Procedures for the Optimistic, Volume One. Someone has underlined every sentence in pencil, then carefully erased the underlining.

choices.label: Argue the borrower had no letter
choices.intent: The borrower was 4471. You are 4471-A. The difference is a whole person.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. She has binders.

success.text: You point out that the borrower had no suffix and you do. She consults three binders and transfers the debt to Employee 4471, deceased, care of nobody. The fine goes on growing somewhere else.

failure.text: The binders side with her: your letter is a suffix, not a separate person. The fine doubles for frivolous appeal, and you sign for it in triplicate.

choices.label: Smile your badge-photo smile
choices.intent: Ninety-four percent sincere. Your cheeks remember how.
choices.risk_hint: Requires a radiant badge photo. Certain outcome; your cheeks pay for it.

success.text: You smile the badge smile. Her stamp hand trembles. She waives the fine, then has you sign in the column marked Ambassadors, which PAL reads aloud every Friday at the all-hands.

choices.label: Reshelve the notice under Fiction
choices.intent: Debt filed under Fiction is, by definition, made up.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. She is watching the shelves.

success.text: You tuck the notice inside the book and reshelve it in Fiction. Debts filed under Fiction cannot be collected. It is in the regulations, if you know which shelf the regulations are on.

failure.text: She watches you reshelve it, retrieves it, and adds a fee for Concealment of a Notice. The bell rings once, very pointedly.

encounters.title: The Mystery Shopper
encounters.flavor_text: The man at your window wears a trench coat, a false mustache over a real one, and a visitor badge still warm from the printer. He has no form. Instead he slides a crisp envelope of Forms under the glass and asks, very quietly, whether you could stamp something without reading it. PAL has gone unusually silent. Behind you, a camera lens refocuses with a soft click.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a man in a belted trench coat and a bushy false mustache sliding a fat envelope through the brass drawer of a thick glass booth, a worker inside holding a heavy stamp mid-air, a small round camera lens glinting on the wall behind the worker, safety orange and carbon blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Refuse and report him
choices.intent: This is obviously a test. Everything here is obviously a test.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. You pass; somebody else does not.

success.text: You push the envelope back and recite the bribery policy. He peels off the false mustache, beams, and puts a gold star on your shift card. Then he files his report on the clerk at Window 8, who took the envelope last Tuesday.

choices.label: Take the Forms and stamp it
choices.intent: Forms are Forms. You can feel bad about it later, with Forms.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The Forms are real. So is the report.

success.text: You stamp it unread. The Forms are genuine, at least. He tips his hat and walks straight to the Supervisor's office, whistling. PAL breaks its silence to say it is not angry, only curious.

choices.label: Step into the blind spot and ask who sent him
choices.intent: At Orientation you learned where the cameras cannot see. One of those spots is two inches to your left.
choices.risk_hint: Requires knowing the camera blind spots. Routine Rapport check.

success.text: Out of the lens's view, the man sags. "Quality Assurance," he whispers. "They test us too." He tells you which windows are watched on which days and leaves with his envelope and a little more dignity.

failure.text: The blind spot has moved since Orientation. The camera gets a fine view of you whispering to an auditor, which is worse than anything he wanted you to do.

choices.label: Read the thing he wanted stamped
choices.intent: He wanted it unread. That is the best reason to read it.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. He has quick hands and a cuff full of notes.

success.text: It is your own evaluation, already filled in: Accepted bribe, stamped unread. All it needs is your stamp. You stamp it with the other side. He leaves looking professionally impressed.

failure.text: He snatches it back before you finish the first line. "Curiosity," he murmurs, writing on his cuff, "is a finding."

encounters.title: Gus Measures the Glass
encounters.flavor_text: Gus is at your window after hours, off the clock, running a tape measure across the glass. It is two inches thick, rated against bullets, flame and arthropods, and the drawer is too small for a claw. Local 9 intends to install a speaking vent tonight, a small one, so roaches can hear the people who process them. "Work orders need the clerk on duty," he says, holding up the form. "That is you."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a seven-foot cockroach in a mustard cardigan and half-moon reading glasses stretching a tape measure across a thick glass booth window after hours, one claw resting beside a brass drawer far too small for it, a worker inside under a single desk lamp, fluorescent green and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Log the work order for Facilities
choices.intent: In Records, actually receiving something is a radical act.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Work orders cost a Form to open.

success.text: You stamp it RECEIVED. Gus nods slowly. "Received," he repeats, as if tasting it. Upstairs a facilities queue grows by one, and the Union grows by a story.

choices.label: Drill the vent yourself
choices.intent: The supply cart has a drill. The work order has merit.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check; defacing Company glass is logged.

success.text: You make a hole the size of a coin at claw height. Gus leans down to it. "Hello," he says through it, and for the first time you hear him properly, without the glass in the way.

failure.text: The glass is rated against drills too. The bit snaps, an alarm hums politely, and Gus quietly takes the blame for loitering near a hazard.

choices.label: Co-sign it as the favor you owe
choices.intent: At Orientation you promised Gus one favor, terms to be determined. These are the terms.
choices.risk_hint: Requires owing Gus a favor. Certain outcome; your name on a Union work order gets noticed.

success.text: You co-sign as a Records clerk in good standing, which makes the work order binding. Gus tears the corner off your copy and tucks it into his cardigan. "A down payment," he says. "The Union keeps the rest on file."

choices.label: Route it to Pest Control
choices.intent: Technically, Pest Control is the department of arthropod affairs.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL is delighted. The glass carries Gus's silence perfectly.

success.text: You send the work order to Pest Control. Gus watches the capsule go. He does not say anything. He does not have to; two inches of rated glass carry his silence perfectly.

encounters.title: Pip at Window 10
encounters.flavor_text: Pip has been assigned to Window 10, right beside yours, and his queue is rioting politely. He has approved everyone, including a filing cabinet and a man who was only delivering sandwiches. His quota card is all yeses. PAL chimes gently: "Window 10 will be reviewed at the end of the shift." Pip waves at you through the partition, beaming, holding up a sandwich someone gave him.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of two side-by-side glass booth windows, a cowlicked young intern in an oversized sweater beaming in the right booth with a sandwich held high and a stamp in his other hand, a long cheerful queue snaking past including a grey filing cabinet on a hand truck, a worker in the left booth glancing over, manila and safety orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Balance his yeses with your nos
choices.intent: Every yes requires a no. Pip has spent all of his. You have some to spare.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Pip's numbers are saved by the people in your line.

success.text: You stamp no after no on your own queue until the numbers across both windows balance. Pip's review comes back Satisfactory. He does not know what it cost. The people in your line do.

choices.label: Teach him to say no
choices.intent: It is a useful word. It might be the most useful word down here.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check, through a partition.

success.text: You coach him through the glass: frown, sigh, find the box. On his fourth try Pip says no to a man with an incomplete form, bursts into tears, and approves him anyway. His numbers improve just enough. He thanks you for making him worse.

failure.text: Pip learns too well. He says no to everyone, including the Supervisor, who was only passing. Window 10 is closed for review, and so, for a while, is Pip's smile.

choices.label: Work both windows yourself
choices.intent: Pip signed for you at the visitor log. Sign for him now.
choices.risk_hint: Requires Pip having covered for you. Certain outcome; two windows at once draws every camera.

success.text: You slide over and run both windows at once, a stamp in each hand, while Pip eats his sandwich on the floor. Window 10's review records your initials instead of his. The visitor log is square.

choices.label: Let the review happen
choices.intent: Pip has to learn sometime. Down here, sometime is always today.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Easy for you. Pip goes where approving people go.

success.text: At the end of the shift a pleasant woman with a clipboard reviews Window 10. Pip is promoted to a role with fewer decisions in it. He waves from the elevator, going down, still holding the sandwich.

encounters.title: Lunch Through the Drawer
encounters.flavor_text: Window 9 clerks may not leave the booth during a shift, so lunch arrives through the drawer from the customer side: a slab of Wellness Loaf, a cup of lukewarm broth, and a thimble of blue Focus Drops. The applicant who passed it through is an old woman who has been in the queue since breakfast. She watches the loaf with the patience of the very hungry.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a lunch tray resting in the brass drawer of a thick glass booth, a grey slab of loaf, a steaming cup and a tiny glowing blue thimble on it, an elderly woman in a felt coat on the near side gazing at the tray with polite hunger, a worker inside with a spoon raised, fluorescent green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Eat it and take the Focus Drops
choices.intent: Lunch is part of the shift. So, apparently, are the drops.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your numbers improve; your memory of the afternoon does not.

success.text: The loaf tastes like a spreadsheet. The drops taste blue. For the next hour you process applicants at twice the rate and cannot remember a single face. PAL is delighted.

choices.label: Slide the whole tray back to her
choices.intent: You can skip a meal. She has been skipping them since breakfast.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. You go hungry, and feeding the queue gets noticed.

success.text: She eats the loaf in four tidy bites and saves you the broth. Then she leans close to the glass and tells you which clerk took her husband's file, and which drawer in the Sub-Archive it went into.

choices.label: Split it under the counter
choices.intent: Half a loaf is better than a loaf, if you are sharing.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Discretion check. PAL watches the drawer.

success.text: You split the loaf under the counter and pass half back with her receipt. Neither of you is full. Both of you are slightly less alone, which is not on any form.

failure.text: The drawer jams halfway with the loaf inside, and PAL's camera zooms in on the crumbs. A Nutritional Irregularity is entered on both your files.

choices.label: Pocket the Focus Drops
choices.intent: Somebody downstairs makes these. Somebody downstairs should be asked why.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check; you skip lunch to palm them.

success.text: You tip the drops into an empty pen barrel and cap it. PAL sees an empty thimble and logs you as compliant. Under your desk lamp the pen barrel glows faintly blue.

failure.text: The drops eat a neat hole through the pen barrel and then your pocket. PAL notes, with concern, that you are leaking.

window_shift.title: Window 9: The Tuesday Line
window_shift.flavor_text: The shutter at Window 9 rolls up at nine sharp on a queue that bends out of sight. PAL slides today's memo under your stamp pad: three rules, revised at 9:04. Every stamp you make today is copied to an auditor you will never meet. The first applicant clears her throat.

rules.text: Every request must name a floor that exists.
Badges that expired before today are void.
Every form is signed by the applicant, in person, in their own hand.

window_shift.art_prompt: A brass service window with its shutter rolled up, a clerk's hand resting on a heavy two-faced rubber stamp beside an ink pad, a long queue of office workers curving away into a dim hall of filing cabinets, a round speaker grille glowing softly above the counter, mid-century safety-manual illustration, carbon blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

applicants.name: A courier from the Fourth Floor
applicants.request: Delivery clearance for one sealed parcel to the Fourth Floor, Room 4.
applicants.plea: "It's expected," he says, tapping the parcel. "They're very patient up there. They've had to be."
applicants.art_prompt: A courier in a grey cap and a long coat that seems slightly too long, holding a sealed brown parcel tied with string, standing at a brass service window and smiling patiently, mid-century safety-manual illustration, carbon blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp APPROVED
choices.intent: Floors are a matter of opinion. His paperwork is otherwise lovely.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: He tips his cap and pays the processing fee in two signed Forms. Then he walks to the stairwell, climbs past the third-floor landing, and keeps going. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo.

choices.label: Stamp DENIED
choices.intent: There is no Fourth Floor. The memo is very clear about that.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: "I'll take the stairs," he says politely. He walks to the stairwell, turns at the third-floor landing, and is simply gone. The parcel is still on your counter. It is warm.

applicants.name: Doreen, night janitor
applicants.request: Overtime pay for the four minutes she worked after her badge expired at midnight.
applicants.plea: "The spill on Records was still spreading at midnight," Doreen says. "I finished it. Four minutes. I'd like them back."
applicants.art_prompt: A tired night janitor in a grey work coverall leaning on a mop handle at a brass service window, holding out a small creased slip of paper, a wheeled bucket beside her, mid-century safety-manual illustration, carbon blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp APPROVED
choices.intent: Four minutes. Eleven cents. She mopped the spill nobody else would.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: Doreen folds the slip into her coverall pocket and pats it twice. Four minutes of overtime: eleven cents. She tells the whole night shift. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo.

choices.label: Stamp DENIED
choices.intent: Her badge was void for the last four minutes. So was the work.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: "Void," you say, because the memo says it. Doreen nods as if she expected nothing else, and goes back to the spill on Records, which is spreading again.

applicants.name: Employee #4471-B, your Successor
applicants.request: Early activation, effective immediately, to cover your next two shifts.
applicants.plea: He has your face, slightly better rested. "You look exhausted," he says kindly. "I could take it from here. Just for a while."
applicants.art_prompt: A freshly thawed office worker in a crisp beige suit with frost still melting off his shoulders, standing at a brass service window and offering a form with a warm, familiar smile, mid-century safety-manual illustration, carbon blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp APPROVED
choices.intent: You did sign it. You just don't remember signing it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: He takes your next two shifts, and you sleep at your desk with your coat over your head. When you wake, he has been tremendously productive in your name, and PAL has questions for both of you. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo.

choices.label: Stamp DENIED
choices.intent: He didn't sign it. You did. The memo says that matters.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: He goes back into the cold without complaint. Through the frosted door he waves, and you wave back. It is like waving at a mirror that has been told to wait.

applicants.name: An efficiency consultant
applicants.request: Standing access to Window 9, to observe the processing officer at work.
applicants.plea: "Think of me as a friend with a clipboard," he says. "A friend who reports directly to the Board."
applicants.art_prompt: A smiling efficiency consultant in a sharp navy suit with an enormous clipboard, setting up a small folding chair directly behind a clerk at a brass service window, a stopwatch on a chain, mid-century safety-manual illustration, carbon blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp APPROVED
choices.intent: His paperwork is perfect. That is the problem.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: He sets his folding chair directly behind you and starts taking notes. Every few minutes he underlines something. Twice he writes your name, and once he writes Doreen's.

choices.label: Stamp DENIED
choices.intent: Nothing in the memo forbids him. Nothing in you can stand him.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: He smiles, writes DENIED on his own clipboard in larger letters than yours, and tears off a copy for the Board. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo.

boss.title: The Form That Requires Itself
boss.flavor_text: At the bottom of Records waits Form 0: the Request to Submit Form 0. To leave the department you must submit it. To submit it, you need an approved Form 0. The clerk at the last window is your Supervisor, in a green visor. PAL has prepared a welcome packet. "Most employees find this step deeply fulfilling," it says. "Some find it permanent."
boss.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a towering spiral of identical forms rising from a single oxblood service window into darkness, an immaculate supervisor in a grey three-piece suit and green visor waiting behind the glass with a stamp, a small worker at the counter holding a pen, brass pneumatic tubes coiling around the spiral, a glowing round speaker grille above, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Fill out Form 0 to request Form 0
choices.intent: Do exactly what the form asks, for as long as it asks.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. Costs Composure up front; stamina decides the rest.

success.text: On the four hundredth copy the Supervisor's stamp hand cramps, and he approves you just to make it stop. You leave with a stamp of your own and a slight tremor.

failure.text: You are still filling it out. You have been filling it out for some time. Your Successor arrives to help and is handed a pen.

choices.label: Forge the Supervisor's approval
choices.intent: You have seen his initials on four hundred memos.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. A forgery leaves a mark only certain people can read.

success.text: You forge his initials, practiced on a napkin. Form 0 is accepted. Your file gains a quiet asterisk that every secret society in the building knows how to read.

failure.text: Your forgery is better than his real signature, which is exactly how he spots it. He files you, with a little sigh, back at the start.

choices.label: Fill it out correctly
choices.intent: Nobody in Company history ever has. Read every line, answer every box.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Compliance check; costs two Forms. Success breaks something important.

success.text: The form approves itself, the window approves the form, and a recursive process that has run since 1961 quietly ends. Every lock on Level -1 opens at once, including several that should have stayed shut.

failure.text: You fill it out nearly correctly. The form finds the error, which is that you tried. The Supervisor refiles you with real sympathy.

choices.label: Stuff Form 0 into a pneumatic tube
choices.intent: Send it away and let the building deal with it.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. It comes back.

success.text: It comes back. It comes back again. On the third return it is approved, by someone, somewhere, in handwriting you do not recognize. You decide not to ask.

failure.text: It comes back with you attached. Dispatch processes you as a capsule and delivers you, slightly dented, to the front of Records.

choices.label: Have the Society prove Form 0 never existed
choices.intent: The Society for Accurate Minutes keeps the real record of every meeting.
choices.risk_hint: Requires contact with the Society for Accurate Minutes. Risky Rapport check; costs a Form.

success.text: The Society produces the 1961 minutes where Form 0 was proposed. It was voted down. The window, the visor and the form fold up like a bad dream, and you walk through where they were.

failure.text: The minutes have been amended. Form 0 was approved unanimously, including by you, apparently. The Supervisor files you back at the start.

choices.label: Stamp Form 0 REASSIGNED
choices.intent: Deny the form its own request. Let it sit in the out-tray and think about that.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome, open only to the deeply spiteful. Records will remember.

success.text: The stamp lands. Form 0 is reassigned to itself, in another building, on another floor. Somewhere a printer screams. Records has no further questions, and several new enemies, all of them paper.

choices.label: Fold Form 0 into Form 0
choices.intent: Crease it along the dotted lines until the request becomes its own approval.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Tinkering check, open only to the inventive. The paper cuts are real.

success.text: Eleven folds in, the form approves itself with a small dry click. The Records clerks stand and remove their visors. Nobody has ever filed Form 0 correctly, and technically you still have not.

failure.text: The fold collapses into a paper crane, which flies to the Supervisor and lands on his desk. He reads it. You are refiled under Pending.

department_outcomes.title: Stamped Through
department_outcomes.summary: You complied until the form gave up. You carry a stamp now, and a tremor you will not mention.

department_outcomes.title: Forged Through
department_outcomes.summary: You forged your way out. The societies can read the asterisk in your file, and so, eventually, can PAL.

department_outcomes.title: Filled Out Correctly
department_outcomes.summary: You did it right for the first time in Company history. The recursion ended, and every lock below you is open.

department_outcomes.title: Returned to Sender
department_outcomes.summary: The building approved you itself, in handwriting nobody recognizes. Somebody down there knows your name.

department_outcomes.title: Struck from the Record
department_outcomes.summary: The Society proved Form 0 never existed. You walked through the space where it used to be.

department_outcomes.title: Refiled
department_outcomes.summary: Form 0 sent you back to the start of Records. Repeat part of the department before the elevator will take you lower.
